extracted.intended_audience: Principal Investigators and organizational representatives preparing pre‑applications and full applications for the CDMRP FY24 PRCRP Idea Award (Department of Defense funding applicants)
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of a two‑step (pre‑application and invited full application) grant application to the CDMRP FY24 Peer Reviewed Cancer Research Program (Idea Award), meeting programmatic topic/focus requirements, formatting, eligibility, and administrative rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must address at least one FY24 PRCRP Topic Area
rubrics_metrics.description: To be considered for funding, applications for the FY24 PRCRP Idea Award must address at least one of the congressionally directed FY24 PRCRP Topic Areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FY24 PRCRP Topic Areas include: Bladder cancer; Germ cell cancers; Neuroblastoma; Blood cancers; Liver cancer; Brain cancer (excluding glioblastoma); Lymphoma; Colorectal cancer; Endometrial cancer; Esophageal cancer; Mesothelioma; Metastatic cancers; Myeloma; Pediatric, adolescent, and young adult cancers; Pediatric brain tumors; Stomach cancer; Sarcoma; Thyroid cancer. Applications that do not address at least one listed Topic Area will be administratively withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Congressional exclusions on cancer types
rubrics_metrics.description: FY24 PRCRP must not address research in melanoma, glioblastoma, or cancers originating in the breast, pancreas, prostate, ovary, kidney, or lung; funds must not be used to study rare cancers (except relevant subtypes of allowed Topic Areas).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that include excluded cancer types (primary breast, kidney, lung, pancreatic, prostate, ovarian, melanoma, glioblastoma, or non‑allowed rare cancers) as part of the research study will be administratively withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must address at least one FY24 PRCRP Military Health Focus Area
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must define how the research is relevant to Service Members and their Families by addressing at least one FY24 PRCRP Military Health Focus Area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus Areas include: Environmental exposure risk factors associated with cancer (must be relevant to military activities/deployments); Mission readiness and gaps in cancer research (gaps in prevention, detection, prognosis, treatment, survivorship, quality of life that impact mission readiness). Applicants must demonstrate how proposed research will decrease the burden of cancer on Service Members, Veterans, beneficiaries, and/or the American public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental/occupational exposure relevance
rubrics_metrics.description: Environmental and/or occupational risk factors should be relevant to activities specific to the military (e.g., deployments leading to exposures to ionizing radiation, chemicals, infectious agents, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should refer to VA and PRCRP exposure resources. Studies should tie exposures directly to military contexts and explain relevance to Service Member health and mission readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mission readiness relevance and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Research must address gaps that may impact mission readiness or health/well‑being of military members and beneficiaries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: studies improving survival while minimizing late effects to allow return to duty; therapeutics that minimize time in treatment; methods to minimize relapse; improvements in early detection leading to earlier diagnosis and return to duty. Describe clear linkage to mission readiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Must address at least one FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must address at least one of the 17 FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenges (classified into five categories) and not just select a category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overarching Challenges categories: Prevention; Diagnostics/Prognostics; Therapeutics; Patient Well‑Being and Survivorship; Disparity. Within each category, applicants must identify a specific challenge (e.g., investigate prevention interventions; develop minimally invasive detection methods; transform treatment for advanced disease; study survivorship/quality of life interventions; improve care/accessibility for underserved populations) and describe how the work can lead to a breakthrough or major impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Idea Award intent: innovative, high‑risk/high‑reward basic research
rubrics_metrics.description: The FY24 PRCRP Idea Award supports innovative, untested, high‑risk/potentially high‑reward concepts, theories, paradigms, and/or basic cancer research that may introduce a new paradigm or challenge existing paradigms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The award is intended for highly creative ideas, not incremental or logical next steps. The proposed research should include a well‑formulated, testable hypothesis based on strong scientific rationale and study design and aim to generate robust preliminary data for future projects. Incremental advances or simply switching model systems are not considered innovative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary data discouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Inclusion of preliminary data is discouraged because the award is not intended to support ongoing research in the applicant’s laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not consistent with the exploratory nature of this award and applicants should avoid emphasizing extensive preliminary results; advanced projects with robust preliminary data may be more appropriate for the Impact Award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clinical trials prohibited; clinical research allowed (observational)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clinical trials are not allowed under this funding opportunity. Clinical research that is observational in nature and does not assess safety/effectiveness/efficacy of interventions is allowed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clinical trial definition per 45 CFR 46.102 cited. Allowed clinical research examples: mechanisms of human disease; diagnostic/detection studies (biomarker or imaging); health disparity studies; development of new technologies; epidemiologic and behavioral studies not assessing intervention outcomes; outcomes and health services research not meeting clinical trial definition. Research that prospectively assigns human subjects to evaluate interventions (including placebos) is a clinical trial and is disallowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant and organization eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible applicants include extramural and intramural organizations (foreign or domestic, for‑profit and non‑profit, public entities). Awards are made to organizations, not individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extramural organizations are non‑DOD entities (academia, industry, foundations, non‑DOD federal orgs). Intramural refers to DOD organizations (DOD labs, DOD military treatment facilities). Refer to General Application Instructions for recipient qualification requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator eligibility and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: PI must have a faculty‑level appointment or equivalent and be employed by or affiliated with an eligible organization; each investigator may be named as PI on only one Idea Award pre‑application or application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators may be co‑PI or collaborator on multiple submissions but only PI on one Idea Award. PI changes are not allowed except in extenuating circumstances evaluated case‑by‑case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and period of performance constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: The anticipated direct costs budget for the entire period of performance should not exceed $400,000 for an Idea Award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section II.D.5 Funding Restrictions for details. Awards supported with FY24 funds will be made no later than Sept 30, 2025. CDMRP expects to allot approximately $16M to fund approximately 20 Idea Award applications; funding is contingent upon availability and program requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑step submission process and invitation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission requires pre‑application via eBRAP and, if invited, a full application (via eBRAP or Grants.gov depending on extramural vs intramural). An invitation to submit a full application is required; full applications without invitation will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eBRAP assigns a unique log number during pre‑application required for full application. Pre‑application contents (title, PI, org info) must be consistent across pre and full application. Start submission early; no grace periods for deadlines. Extramural full applications must be submitted through Grants.gov; intramural may use eBRAP or Grants.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preproposal Narrative content and one‑page limit (pre‑application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Preproposal Narrative must be a single page (text and non‑text elements included) and must include specified elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preproposal must: state FY24 PRCRP Topic Area(s); describe rationale and hypothesis and how they support objectives and specific aims; describe methodology and experimental design support; explain how project is innovative; explain how research will lead to promising outcomes for selected Military Health Focus Area(s); state FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge(s) and describe potential for breakthrough/impact. Inclusion of URLs in Preproposal Narrative is prohibited and may result in administrative withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑application supporting documentation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑application supporting documents must be uploaded as separate PDF files with limits (References Cited one page; Key Personnel biosketches five pages each combined into one file; list of abbreviations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References Cited (1 page) must use a standard format; key personnel biosketches should demonstrate background/expertise; upload as a single combined file. Do not include additional unrequested documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre‑application screening criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre‑applications will be screened on technical merit and relevance to DHP and PRCRP using explicit criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Screening criteria include: whether proposed project addresses at least one FY24 PRCRP Topic Area; how well the rationale/hypothesis support objectives and specific aims; whether methodology/experimental design support project goals; whether proposed research is innovative; degree to which research may lead to promising outcomes for selected Military Health Focus Area(s); whether an FY24 PRCRP Overarching Challenge is to be studied and to what degree the research will lead to a breakthrough or make an impact. No feedback/critique provided at this stage; invited full applications should maintain title/objectives from pre‑application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative content and six‑page limit (full application)
rubrics_metrics.description: Attachment 1 Project Narrative must be up to six pages and describe the proposed project using a specified outline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Narrative must include: Hypothesis or Objective; Rationale; Specific Aims; Relevance to the Idea Award Intent (explain how project is innovative and exploratory); Research Strategy (experimental design, methods, analyses, controls, statistical plan and power analysis if applicable, description of human subject population and access, potential pitfalls and alternatives, demonstration of availability of tissue/data). If human subjects/specimens used, include recruitment/acquisition plan and document PI/colleagues' experience. Discouraged: preliminary data. Include inclusion of women/minorities strategy and justification for exclusions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attachment 2: Supporting Documentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting Documentation (Support.pdf) must combine specific documents; it must not include figures/tables/graphs/photographs/diagrams/chemical structures or drawings (those belong in Project Narrative).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include References Cited (no page limit unless noted), List of Abbreviations/Acronyms/Symbols, Facilities/Equipment/Resources descriptions, Publications/Patents (list relevant URLs/abstracts; up to five published manuscripts can be included if not publicly available). Start each document on a new page. Inclusion of unrequested items may be removed or cause administrative withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required attachments and naming conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Full applications must include specified attachments uploaded as individual files with exact filenames.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Project Narrative as 'ProjectNarrative.pdf' (Attachment 1); Supporting Documentation 'Support.pdf' (Attachment 2); Technical Abstract 'TechAbs.pdf' (Attachment 3); Lay Abstract 'LayAbs.pdf' (Attachment 4); Statement of Work 'SOW.pdf' (Attachment 5); Relevance to Military Health 'MilHealth.pdf' (Attachment 6); Innovation Statement 'Innovation.pdf' (Attachment 7); Impact Statement 'Impact.pdf' (Attachment 8); Representations 'RequiredReps.pdf' (Attachment 9). Follow General Application Instructions formatting (Appendix 2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting and page limit enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Page limits apply to specified documents and will be enforced; pages exceeding limits will be removed or cause administrative rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preproposal Narrative one page; Project Narrative six pages; References, biosketch page limits apply as noted. Pages exceeding limits will be removed prior to review (except Project Narrative where exceeding causes rejection). Documents not requested will be removed and may cause administrative withdrawal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting same research to multiple funding opportunities in same program/fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitting essentially the same research project to different funding opportunities within the same program and fiscal year is prohibited and will result in administrative withdrawal of duplicative application(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unnecessary duplication or accepting funding from more than one source for the same research is prohibited. See CDMRP research duplication policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classified or sensitive research is disallowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Including classified research data or proposing research that may produce classified or national security‑sensitive outcomes may result in application withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to General Application Instructions Appendix 7, Section B. If research may produce classified outcomes, do not include it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict of interest / programmatic panel involvement prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: FY24 PRCRP Programmatic Panel members must not be involved in any pre‑application or full application; naming panel members on applications or involvement will result in withdrawal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panel involvement includes concept design, application development, budget preparation, development of supporting documentation/letters. A list of panel members is provided on the PRCRP website; do not involve or name them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative rejection and withdrawal triggers
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific administrative failures result in rejection or withdrawal of pre‑applications or full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rejection examples: Preproposal Narrative missing or exceeding page limit; more than one pre‑application/application with the same PI. Full application rejection examples: submission without letter of invitation; Project Narrative missing or exceeding page limit; Budget missing. Withdrawal examples: naming programmatic panel members; inclusion of URLs (except in References/Publication sections); contacting reviewers to influence process; proposing clinical trials; failing to address required Topic Area, Military Health Focus Area, or Overarching Challenge; proposing excluded cancers; PI ineligibility; extramural submissions received through eBRAP (instead of Grants.gov).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency requirement between pre‑application and full application
rubrics_metrics.description: Title and research objectives in the full application should not be changed from the pre‑application since invitation is based on pre‑application contents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigators should not change title or research objectives after pre‑application submission; inconsistencies may delay processing and reduce ability to modify/verify application in eBRAP. If changes are necessary, contact eBRAP Help Desk before deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines and no exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: All pre‑ and full application components must be submitted by the deadlines stated; there are no grace periods for deadlines and failure to meet them will result in rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines: Pre‑Application June 21, 2024 5:00 p.m. ET; Invitation Aug 2, 2024; Application Submission Sept 26, 2024 11:59 p.m. ET; End of Verification Oct 1, 2024 5:00 p.m. ET. Start submission early to avoid system errors and interface issues with Grants.gov; USAMRAA cannot make exceptions for system‑to‑system problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portal usage rules (eBRAP and Grants.gov)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use eBRAP for pre‑applications; full applications for extramural organizations must be submitted to Grants.gov; intramural DOD organizations may submit full applications via eBRAP or Grants.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eBRAP is used to receive communications, submit pre‑applications, and verify full applications. Extramural submissions to eBRAP (full application) will be withdrawn. Follow the portal instructions for extramural vs intramural submissions exactly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human subjects/animals/IRB/IACUC compliance and institutional oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications involving animals, human data, human specimens, human subjects, or human cadavers must be reviewed for federal and DOD protections and approved by USAMRDC Office of Human and Animal Research Oversight prior to implementation (in addition to local IRB/IACUC/Ethics reviews).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for human subject recruitment, sample acquisition, and describe regulatory compliance. Refer to General Application Instructions Appendix 6 for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting requirements if funded
rubrics_metrics.description: Awardees must submit annual technical progress reports and a final technical progress report in accordance with the Research Performance Progress Report; an Award Expiration Transition Plan must be submitted with the final progress report.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Award Expiration Transition Plan (one page) must outline whether and how research will progress post‑award and include known or pending funding sources. Additional reporting requirements may apply based on Award Terms and Conditions and recipient integrity/performance disclosures to SAM for organizations with federal awards over $10M.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouragement of collaboration with DOD/VA and multidisciplinary partnerships
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators are strongly encouraged to collaborate, integrate, or align projects with DOD and/or VA research labs and programs; multidisciplinary collaborations among academia, industry, military services, VA, and other federal agencies are highly encouraged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such collaborations can leverage knowledge, infrastructure, and access to unique clinical populations. If relying on unique resources/databases, describe access at submission and plan for maintaining access throughout the research.
